title: Brain manifest
description: The self-description a brain publishes so parents, routers, agents and doctor can reason about it WITHOUT reading its tree. Config (client.config.json) is input; this is the generated declaration of what the instance currently IS: identity, scope, profile composition, engine generation, populated inventory, which projections exist and how far behind canon they are, what it will publish upward, and which surfaces it answers on. Emitted by scripts/gen-manifest.py.

manifest.description: Manifest format contract. Consumers gate on this before reading anything else.

generated.description: ISO date of emission. VOLATILE — this artifact is carved out of the generated-clean drift gate for the same reason activity.json and staleness.json are.

id.description: Instance id — client.slug. The federation namespace this brain's addresses take when it publishes upward.

scope.description: Where this brain sits in the scope spine. Ownership flows down, abstraction flows up, access narrows on the way up.

parent.description: Scope address of the parent brain (`<level>:<id>`), or null for a root.

peers.description: Scope addresses of sibling brains this one federates with laterally.

profile.description: Which ontology this brain composes. `overlays` is ordered; a later overlay may extend but never silently redefine an earlier kind.

declared.description: The legacy single-string `profile` field from brain-schema.json, carried for skew detection until every instance composes.

engine.description: Generation markers. The whole point of the manifest for a fleet at three different generations: skew becomes legible without upgrading anything first.

schema_present.description: Whether the instance carries brain-schema.json at all. False means pre-ontology generation.

gates.description: Gates registered in gates.json; 0 means pre-improvement-graph generation.

template_sync.description: Template sync baseline, when one has been recorded (#52).

inventory.description: What is actually POPULATED, not what is declared. A declared-but-empty kind is the coverage gap a parent needs to know about before it federates.

projections.description: The resolutions this brain can answer at, and how far each has fallen behind canon. Lag is in COMMITS touching canon since the commit that last touched the artifact — null when git cannot say (fail-quiet).

enabled.description: Whether this instance's config turns the resolution on at all.

policy.description: The publish-upward contract. The filter runs HERE, on the way out, because only this brain knows its own tiers.

access_gate.description: Whether an identity-aware access seam (access.js) scopes reads.

publishes.description: Kind ids this brain will hand to its parent. Syntheses and registers, not raw fragments.

withholds.description: Kind ids that never leave this scope, whatever the parent asks for.

surfaces.description: How a caller reaches this brain.

template.description: Active portal template (presentation profile), from portal.template.

federation.description: Children folded in by aggregate-brains.py, when this brain is a metarepo.

substrate.description: How this brain is STORED and DEPLOYED, and what it would take to grow. A brain scales by graduating its substrate, not by rewriting itself: files -> indexed file -> edge database -> server database, with blobs and vectors graduating independently. The manifest reports the current tier and whether the instance has outgrown it, so scaling is a reported condition rather than a discovery made under load.

tier.description: Current canon-projection tier. `files` = app/brain.json in memory; `indexed` = app/brain.db (SQLite + FTS5); `edge-db` = Cloudflare D1; `server-db` = an external database behind the query surface.

store.description: Configured brain.store: json | sqlite | both | d1.

blobs.description: Where non-markdown artifacts live. `git` is correct until it is not; `lfs`/`s3`/`efs` are the graduations. Binary in git is the failure mode this field exists to make visible.

vectors.description: Semantic-resolution substrate. Graduates independently of the node store: a small corpus with heavy semantic search graduates vectors first.

graduation.description: Advisory: has this instance outgrown its tier? Computed from declared thresholds against the live inventory. Advisory ONLY — graduating is a deliberate act with a migration, never automatic.

authority.description: The driver of the adopted brain.authority (files when unset — still un-adopted), or null when this process cannot resolve it (a secret-only dsn, or its env var unset here).

to.description: The next rung of the AUTHORITY ladder (files -> sqlite -> sql), when needed and one exists. Never brain.store's tier — that graduates independently; see `d1` below.

doc.description: Where the hosting/cost model documents this tier's shapes, costs and limits (docs/practices/hosting-models.md).

next_cell.description: The substrate-matrix (#221) authority cell `to` lands on. Null when `to` is null (no adopted-authority ladder available or applicable).

action.description: The exact command that reaches `to`: adopt-first guidance when the authority is still un-adopted, otherwise the tested cross-driver cutover (#227).

d1.description: The D1 projection recommendation at this node count — never a rung of the authority ladder above (D1 is never an authority, ADR #198); it graduates independently, per docs/practices/store-selection.md.

deploy.description: Where this brain runs, and what persistence it is attached to. A brain is portable across targets because canon is git and every projection is rebuildable; the target only decides which projections can exist.

persistence.description: Attached persistence available at the target — what the substrate tiers above are allowed to use.

replicas.description: Declared scale-out width at the target. Read-only replicas are safe at every tier because canon is elsewhere.
